title: Follow the tool
lesson: Propagating trace context connects a tool operation to its agent task on a new run, revealing where time went without making the operation faster.
limitations: Illustrative synchronous scenario and durations; abbreviated trace/span IDs; HTTP client/server intermediary spans omitted.
New run after propagation repair; no retroactive trace reconstruction, performance improvement, correctness or authorization guarantee.
Sampling, export failures, asynchronous links, fan-out and retries are not animated.
Audio analysed for peaks and timing; no physical listening or device audibility review.
Self-reviewed by the author; no comparative recommendation or other variant inspection.

transcript.text: Run A begins. The agent task and model operation share trace 7B but have distinct span IDs. Their connected bars show the model operation taking an illustrative 0.6 seconds.
Trace context is lost at the test-tool boundary. The tool starts separate trace 9C and takes 2.4 seconds. The agent takes 3.0 seconds overall, but its trace does not connect the tool record.

After fixing transport propagation, Run B starts with new trace 8D. The traceparent header crosses the boundary and is extracted by the tool. The tool now shares the agent trace while retaining its own span ID.
A bracket connects the tool interval to the other spans in Run B. The model still takes 0.6 seconds and the tool 2.4 seconds; total duration remains 3.0 seconds.
The tool and its longer interval are highlighted for investigation. Tracing improved visibility, not speed. The scene fades to black. These durations and identifiers are illustrative, not guarantees.
